note: Names, descriptions and grades are exactly as PlayStation publishes them. Hidden flags are this guide's reconstruction of PlayStation's hidden list (28 hidden). Missable is only ever marked 'possible' where a real basis exists; nothing here is presented as a verified missable list.

trophies.guide: The platinum is the reward for the other 54 trophies, so there is no separate trick to it: finish the story, clear the stranger strands, and work through the collectibles, activities and combat feats in the roadmap below. Expect roughly 75 hours for a relaxed first playthrough that mops up as it goes, and treat the two 'possible' missable trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) as the only ones worth doing early, while a partner is around.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
steps: Play the story through to the final mission, earning the chapter and mission trophies as you go.
Finish all eight stranger mission strands and the five character-final trophies in roadmap stage 2.
Clear the activity trophies in stage 3: shooting range golds, races, fishing, arcade and bowling.
Collect everything in stage 4: cards, WAiNK spots, meditation spots, vehicles and all 52 areas.
Sweep up the combat, robbery and economy trophies in stage 5, then check the tracker for the last few stragglers.
When the tracker shows 54 of 54, this platinum pops on its own — no extra step needed.
trophies.tip: Use the tracker's 'Next best trophy' box: it always points at the easiest un-earned trophy, so you never stall deciding what to do next.

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players earn. Follow the on-screen prompts through the opening scene, learn the basic movement and driving controls as the game teaches them, and finish the mission's closing objective. It cannot be missed: the mission is mandatory and the trophy pops at the end of it.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
steps: Start a new game and play through the opening cutscenes until you gain control.
Follow the waypoint marker and the on-screen prompts for movement, sprinting and entering a vehicle.
Complete the fishing beat the mission teaches: cast, wait for the bite, then reel in steadily.
Drive to the mission's closing marker when the objective updates.
Finish the final cutscene and the trophy unlocks as the mission completes.
trophies.tip: Don't rush the tutorial prompts — the reeling and driving basics taught here come back in later missions.

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is the opening stretch of the story. Play its missions in order from the mission markers on the map; side activities are optional at this point, so you can push straight through the story if you want the chapter trophy quickly. The trophy unlocks the moment the chapter's final mission ends.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
steps: Open the map and follow the story mission markers (the lettered icons) in order.
Complete each Chapter 1 mission; the story gates progress, so you cannot skip ahead.
Use the mission's checkpoints if you fail a section — you restart from the last checkpoint, not the mission start.
Keep an eye on the chapter title card: the game tells you when a new chapter begins.
Finish the last mission of Chapter 1 and the trophy pops as the chapter closes.
trophies.tip: Chapter trophies are unmissable and story-gated, so there is no need to replay anything for them.

trophies.guide: Chapter 2 continues directly from Chapter 1, so just keep following the story markers. New areas of Leonida open up as the chapter progresses, and a few new activities unlock along the way — worth a quick try, but none of them is needed for this trophy. Finish the chapter's final mission to unlock it.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
steps: After Chapter 1 ends, follow the new story markers that appear on the map.
Work through Chapter 2's missions in order; each one unlocks the next.
Try any new activity the game introduces, but don't feel obliged to finish it yet.
Stock up on ammo and armour before the chapter's bigger shootouts.
Complete the final mission of Chapter 2 and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Chapter 2 is a good time to start the 'possible' missable trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) while your partner is regularly around.

trophies.guide: Chapter 3 takes the story into Vice City proper. Missions get longer and the shootouts busier, so make a habit of grabbing armour and a full weapon loadout between missions. As with the earlier chapters, the trophy is story-gated and unmissable: finish the chapter's last mission and it pops.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
steps: Follow the story markers into Vice City and play the chapter's missions in order.
Between missions, visit an Ammu-Nation to top up ammo and buy armour.
Use cover and Combat Focus in the bigger gunfights; rushing open ground gets expensive.
Complete the chapter's mid-point missions, which unlock new districts and contacts.
Finish the final mission of Chapter 3 to unlock the trophy.
trophies.tip: Vice City's streets are dense with collectibles — grab WAiNK spots and vehicles as you pass them to save backtracking later.

trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the longest chapter before the finale, with the story's biggest set pieces. Keep your loadout stocked, use the mission checkpoints liberally, and don't be afraid to drop the difficulty of a stubborn section by retrying from a checkpoint with a different approach. The trophy unlocks when the chapter's final mission ends.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
steps: Play Chapter 4's missions in story order from the map markers.
Before the big set-piece missions, buy armour and fill every weapon's ammo.
In vehicle chases, stick to the mission's suggested route rather than cutting across town.
If a mission fails, retry from the checkpoint and change one thing — weapon, route or timing.
Complete the chapter's final mission and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: By now you should have most of the story trophies; check the tracker and mop up any partner-dependent feats before the finale.

trophies.guide: The final mission is the story's last beat and its only gold story trophy. It unlocks after Chapter 4, so you cannot reach it early, and it cannot be missed. Stock up fully before you start — armour, ammo for every weapon, and a fast car — then play it through to the ending cutscene.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
steps: Finish Chapter 4 to unlock the final mission marker.
Buy full armour and max out ammo for your main weapons before starting.
Play the mission in order; it has several phases, each with its own checkpoint.
Use cover and Combat Focus in the final shootout rather than trading shots in the open.
Watch the ending, and the gold trophy unlocks as the credits approach.
trophies.tip: Before the finale, do the two 'possible' missable trophies if you haven't yet — partner availability after the ending is not guaranteed.

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a story mission, so it unlocks in sequence and cannot be missed. Follow the marker to the meeting point, play through the mission's driving and on-foot beats, and finish the closing objective. The trophy pops when the mission completes.
trophies.name: Trust
steps: Wait for the Breakfast Run marker to appear on the map as the story progresses.
Drive to the marker and start the mission.
Follow the on-screen objectives in order, using the waypoint at each step.
Complete the mission's driving section without losing your tail or your cargo.
Finish the closing scene and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Mission trophies are all unmissable — if a mission marker hasn't appeared yet, keep playing the story.

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a story heist mission. It plays in phases — approach, inside work, and the getaway — and each phase has checkpoints. Bring armour and a solid automatic weapon, keep moving during the escape, and the trophy unlocks when the crew gets clear.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
steps: Follow the story to The Cartel Heist marker and start the mission.
Play the approach phase carefully: stay with the crew and follow the prompts.
Inside, grab the objective quickly and watch for the guards the game marks.
During the getaway, follow the escape route and don't stop to fight every pursuer.
Reach the safe point and the trophy unlocks as the mission ends.
trophies.tip: Heist missions are good practice for the robbery trophies later — the same escape discipline applies.

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a story mission that unlocks as the plot develops. Drive to its marker, play through its scenes and objectives in order, and finish the closing beat. Like every mission trophy, it is unmissable once the mission appears.
trophies.name: Family Matters
steps: Continue the story until the Child's Play marker appears.
Start the mission and follow the waypoint through each objective.
Complete any driving or on-foot section the mission asks for.
Use checkpoints if a section fails — you resume close to where you left off.
Finish the final objective and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: If you're hunting efficiently, combine this mission's route with nearby WAiNK and vehicle discoveries.

trophies.guide: Headliners is a story mission with a heavier combat section than most. Stock armour before you start, use cover during the shootout, and let Combat Focus handle the trickier targets. The trophy unlocks when the mission's final objective is done.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
steps: Reach the Headliners marker in the story and start the mission.
Buy armour and ammo first if your stocks are low.
Follow the objectives in order and use cover in the combat sections.
Trigger Combat Focus for the mission's tougher enemies.
Complete the closing objective and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Combat Focus kills here also count toward the Gunslinger trophy if you line up five in one use.

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a story mission set around the airport. Expect a mix of driving, stealthy movement and a shootout, so keep a suppressed option and a loud option in your loadout. Play the objectives in order and the trophy pops at the end.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
steps: Follow the story to the VCIA Takedown marker and start the mission.
Approach the airport area as the mission directs, using stealth where prompted.
Switch to your loud loadout when the mission turns into a firefight.
Complete each objective in order, using checkpoints after any failure.
Finish the final objective and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: The airport is also the place for the 'Catch Me If You Can' trophy — an unscheduled VCIA departure — so remember the layout for later.

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is the toughest of the named story missions, with a long combat sequence and a vehicle section. Go in with full armour, a rifle with plenty of ammo, and a plan to use cover at every step. It is story-gated and unmissable — the trophy pops when the mission's last objective is done.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
steps: Reach the Operation Savage Glory marker and stock up on armour and rifle ammo first.
Play the opening phase as directed, staying with your squad and using cover.
In the long shootout, pick targets from cover and let Combat Focus break the stalemates.
Handle the vehicle section by following the convoy route and keeping your speed up.
Complete the final objective and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: This is the last named mission trophy — after it, only the chapter and finale trophies remain in stage 1.

trophies.guide: 100% Completion is the big gold trophy and the real platinum gate: it means the story, every stranger strand, all the collectibles, activities and side requirements the game counts toward completion. The in-game stats page shows your percentage and what is missing, so check it often. This guide's roadmap is built to cover the same ground — finish stages 1 to 4 and most of stage 5, then use the stats page to find the last few percent.
trophies.name: A Long Road
steps: Finish the full story, including the final mission.
Complete all 8 stranger strands and the character-final missions.
Collect every counted collectible: cards, WAiNK spots, meditation spots and vehicles.
Finish the activity requirements the stats page lists, including races and challenges.
Open the in-game stats page and note the exact categories still below 100%.
Clear the last listed category and the gold trophy unlocks with the 100% mark.
trophies.tip: The stats page is the source of truth for 100% — if the tracker and the game disagree, trust the game's percentage.

trophies.guide: Stunts are the game's airtime and near-miss tricks: jumps, long air, drifts, near misses and wheelies all count, and the game tracks the total. The fastest route is a loop of the big ramps and jumps around Vice City in a fast car or on a bike, chaining jumps and near misses. It is a grind, but it happens naturally if you drive aggressively through the whole game.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
steps: Pick a fast car or a bike and head for the big jumps and ramps around Vice City.
Hit a jump at speed, land cleanly, and keep driving — each jump and long airtime counts.
Chain near misses with traffic between jumps to add stunts without stopping.
Use the stunt jumps the map marks; a clean landing after big air counts more than a small hop.
Repeat the loop until the counter hits 250 — the trophy pops the moment it does.
trophies.tip: Stunts rack up fastest on a bike: jumps, wheelies and near misses chain together between ramps.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Leonida offers nine activity types, and this trophy just asks you to try each one once — no wins or medals needed. The nine are the game's side activities: shooting range, drone racing, street racing, fishing, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting and the WAiNK photo spots. Sample them all and the trophy pops on the ninth.
trophies.name: Master of None
steps: Visit a shooting range and finish any challenge once.
Fly one Top Fun drone race, even if you lose.
Enter and finish any street race, then catch a fish in a challenge against Cal.
Play one arcade game through to its end.
Bowl one frame at the Kolt & Associates alley and meditate at any meditation spot.
Hunt with Bret's strand started, and take a WAiNK photo at one location.
trophies.tip: Do this early: it introduces every activity system, and several of them have their own trophies later.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The Shooting Range has 42 challenges across its weapon categories, and this silver trophy needs a gold medal in every one. Learn each weapon's recoil and the target pattern, take the slow, accurate shots first, and replay a challenge as many times as you need — medals are per-challenge and never expire. This is one of the two hardest silvers, so save it for a focused session.
trophies.name: The Shootist
steps: Visit a shooting range and open the challenge list to see all 42 challenges.
Start with the pistol and rifle challenges to learn the scoring and target timing.
Aim for the head and centre targets first — accuracy beats speed for gold cut-offs.
Replay any challenge that lands silver or bronze until it turns gold.
Work through every weapon category until all 42 show gold, and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Gold cut-offs are tightest on the timed challenges — slow down, breathe, and let the targets settle before each shot.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations across Leonida. You need a win at each one, so learn the racing line, cut the corners through the rings, and use the boost pads the courses place on the fast sections. Races can be retried instantly, so a lost race costs nothing but a minute.
trophies.name: Top Fun
steps: Find a Top Fun drone race marker and start your first race to learn the controls.
Race the course, flying through every ring and hitting the boost pads.
Retry any location you lose — the race restarts instantly with no penalty.
Move to the next location on the map and win there too.
Win at all 14 locations and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: The racing line matters more than top speed: fly the shortest path through the rings and the wins come.

trophies.guide: Street races are scattered across Leonida, and this trophy needs wins in 20 different ones — repeats of the same race do not count. Pick a fast, well-handling car, learn each course's corners, and work through the map's race markers one by one. Any race type counts as long as it is a different race.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
steps: Buy or steal a fast car with good handling and upgrade it if you can.
Open the map and pick the nearest race marker you have not won yet.
Learn the course on the first lap, then push hard on the corners.
Win the race, then move to the next un-won marker.
Win 20 different races and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Keep a list of won races in the tracker notes — the game counts 'different' races, so variety is the whole job.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is the fishing rival, and the challenge is a head-to-head catch contest. Cast where the fish are biting, reel steadily without snapping the line, and land the bigger catch before the timer ends. If Cal wins the first round, challenge him again — the contest can be retried.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
steps: Find Cal at a fishing spot and accept his challenge.
Cast into the marked fishing zone and wait for a bite.
Reel in steadily: ease off when the line strains, pull when the fish tires.
Land a bigger catch than Cal before the challenge timer ends.
Beat him once and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: The line-strain cue is everything: reel hard only when the fish is tired, or the line snaps and the round is lost.

trophies.guide: Arcade cabinets are dotted around Vice City's bars and arcades. Pick any game, play it through to its end — a full run, not just a credit — and the trophy pops. It is one of the quickest trophies in the list and a good first activity trophy.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
steps: Find an arcade cabinet in a bar or arcade in Vice City.
Start any game on the cabinet.
Play the game through to its completion screen.
If you lose a run, start again — progress is per completed game.
Finish one full game and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Pick the shortest game on the cabinet if you only want the trophy; the longer ones are for fun, not for this pop.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of the stranger characters with a multi-mission strand. His missions appear as you explore, so keep an eye out for his marker between story missions, play each of his missions in order, and finish the last one. The trophy pops when his strand closes.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
steps: Find Andy's stranger marker on the map and start his first mission.
Complete each of Andy's missions in order as new markers appear.
Between his missions, play the story on — his later missions unlock as the game progresses.
Stock up before his final mission, which is the longest of the strand.
Complete Andy's final mission and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Stranger strands unlock gradually — if Andy's next marker isn't there yet, push the story forward a chapter.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand is another multi-mission stranger story, this one built around boats and the water. Play his missions in order as they appear, finish the last one, and the trophy pops. His missions are a good excuse to learn the boat handling you'll want for the exploration trophies.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
steps: Find Kenton's stranger marker and start his first mission.
Play each of Kenton's missions in order as they unlock.
Use the boat sections to learn the waterways around the Leonida Keys.
Keep armour and a rifle handy for the strand's rougher missions.
Complete Kenton's final mission and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Kenton's boat missions double as a tour of the Keys — note the WAiNK spots you pass for the collectible sweep.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand is the biker strand: fast rides, highway chases and a final mission that leans on your riding skill. Play his missions in order, keep a good bike in your garage, and finish his last mission for the trophy.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
steps: Find Billy's stranger marker and start his first mission.
Complete each of Billy's missions in order as new markers appear.
Keep a fast bike handy — his missions reward good riding.
Use the highway routes and avoid heavy traffic in the chase sections.
Complete Billy's final mission and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Billy's missions are the best place to build stunt count for the Cunning Stunts trophy — ride hard between objectives.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eight stranger strands are spread across Leonida, each a short chain of missions for a named character. This silver trophy pops when the eighth strand closes. Work the strands between story chapters — their markers appear as you explore — and use the roadmap's stage 2 checklist to see which strands are done. The five character-final trophies are part of the same eight.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
steps: Explore Leonida between story missions and watch for stranger markers on the map.
Start every strand you find and play its missions in order.
Check the stage 2 checklist in the roadmap to see which strands are still open.
Push the story forward if a strand's next mission hasn't appeared yet.
Close the eighth strand and the silver trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Strands unlock with story progress, so don't grind them all at once — weave them through chapters 2 to 4.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand is a supply-and-demand story of moving goods around the state. Play his missions in order as they appear, keep a sturdy vehicle ready for the delivery legs, and finish his final mission for the trophy.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
steps: Find Randy's stranger marker and start his first mission.
Complete each of Randy's missions in order as they unlock.
Keep a fast, sturdy car ready for the delivery and escape legs.
Watch for the ambush beats in his later missions and use cover.
Complete Randy's final mission and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Randy's delivery routes pass several collectible areas — grab the cards and WAiNK spots on the way.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's strand closes with a spin — a driving-heavy finale that rewards clean handling. Play his missions in order, keep your best-handling car in the garage, and finish the last mission for the trophy.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
steps: Find Tyrone's stranger marker and start his first mission.
Play each of Tyrone's missions in order as they appear.
Keep a good-handling car ready for his driving-heavy missions.
In the finale, drive cleanly and follow the route markers rather than improvising.
Complete Tyrone's final mission and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Tyrone's missions are another easy source of stunt count — drift the corners and take the jumps on the way.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: There are 18 meditation spots across Leonida — quiet overlooks, beaches and hilltops marked on the map once you get close. Visit each one, sit down and complete the short meditation, and the trophy pops at the eighteenth. It pairs naturally with the exploration sweep for all 52 areas.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
steps: Open the map and note the meditation markers in each region.
Travel to the nearest unvisited spot and walk into the marked circle.
Start the meditation and let the short sequence play out.
Move to the next spot, working region by region so none is missed.
Meditate at all 18 spots and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Do the meditation spots during the 52-area exploration sweep — the routes overlap and you save hours.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret's strand is the hunting one: track a unique animal through the Leonida wilderness, take the shot cleanly, and bring the proof back. The hunt needs patience — move slowly, watch the wind and the animal's tracks, and don't spook it. The trophy pops when Bret accepts the hunt.
trophies.name: Fair Game
steps: Find Bret's stranger marker and start his strand.
Follow the hunting tutorial: tracks, scent and the animal's trail.
Move slowly and stay downwind so the animal doesn't bolt.
Take the shot when you have a clear, close line — a clean kill matters.
Return to Bret and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Crouch and move slowly in the final approach; sprinting near the animal ends the hunt and wastes the trip.

trophies.guide: Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida in packs, and a set is a complete group of cards. You need three full sets for this silver trophy. Cards are tucked into shops, hideouts and landmarks, so search thoroughly and use the tracker's count to know how many sets you have finished. It is a long hunt — save it for the stage 4 collectible sweep.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
steps: Search interiors, shops and landmarks for card packs as you explore.
Collect every pack you find — the game tracks sets automatically.
Check your collection to see which sets are closest to complete.
Target the missing cards of your nearest sets first.
Complete 3 full sets and the silver trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Cards hide in plain sight on shelves and counters — check every interior you enter during the story.

trophies.guide: WAiNK is the in-game photo mode: at 100 marked locations across Leonida, take a WAiNK photo and the spot counts. The locations cover landmarks, viewpoints and street scenes, so this trophy is really an excuse to tour the whole state. Work region by region and the count climbs fast.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
steps: Open the WAiNK app and check the location list for your region.
Travel to the nearest un-photographed location marker.
Frame the landmark and take the WAiNK photo.
Confirm the spot counts, then move to the next marker.
Photograph 100 locations and the silver trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: WAiNK spots cluster around landmarks — clear a whole district's spots in one drive instead of criss-crossing the map.

trophies.guide: Challenges are the game's small feats — driving, shooting, flying and exploration tasks that the game tracks in the challenges menu. Fifty of them need completing, and they accumulate naturally if you play broadly: stunts, races, hunting and combat all feed the list. Check the menu to see which ones are closest and finish those first.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
steps: Open the challenges menu and see which challenges are nearest to done.
Finish the easy ones first: short drives, simple stunts and quick activities.
Keep playing broadly — races, stunts and combat all feed the challenge list.
Revisit the menu regularly and target the next closest challenges.
Complete 50 challenges and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Challenges overlap with almost every other trophy — don't grind them alone; let them fill in as you play.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This is one of the two trophies this guide flags as possibly missable, because it needs your partner beside you — and partner availability is tied to the story. While your partner is around, build a 4-star wanted level together, then lose the cops and escape. Do it during the story, not after the finale, when partner missions may no longer be available.
trophies.name: Hot Together
steps: Start this during the story, while partner missions are still available.
With your partner beside you, commit crimes until the wanted level hits 4 stars.
Break line of sight: drive into alleys, switch cars, or hide until the search circle shrinks.
Stay hidden until the wanted level clears completely.
Escape with your partner and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Do this in Chapter 2 or 3 while your partner is regularly in missions — after the finale, the chance may be gone.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: This is the second trophy flagged as possibly missable, for the same reason: it needs your partner, and it needs three shop robberies in a row without the wanted level ever dropping. Plan a route with three close shops, rob them one after another, and keep moving so the cops stay on you the whole time.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
steps: Do this during the story while your partner is available for missions.
Pick three shops close together and plan the route between them.
Rob the first shop with your partner, then drive straight to the second.
Rob the second and third without letting the wanted level clear.
Finish the third robbery with the wanted level still active and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Keep the wanted level alive on purpose: don't hide between shops, and don't let the cops lose you until all three are done.

trophies.guide: Leonida is full of vehicles, and this trophy counts the distinct ones you discover — driving a new model for the first time adds it to the list. Cruise the districts, try everything from scooters to trucks, and the count climbs. It pairs well with the Scooter Bros registrations and the garage purchases.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
steps: Drive through a new district and hop into any vehicle model you haven't driven.
Check the vehicle list to see how many distinct models you have found.
Visit the docks, the airport and the countryside for the rarer models.
Try bikes, boats and trucks as well as cars — all of them count.
Discover 100 distinct vehicles and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Every new model counts the first time you drive it — even a 30-second hop in a parked scooter adds to the total.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus slows time and lets you line up shots. To take down five enemies in one use, you need a crowded fight: trigger it when a group is clustered, and drop them one by one before the focus ends. Story shootouts with packed rooms are the best place to try it.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
steps: Find a mission or free-roam fight with a group of clustered enemies.
Wait until at least five enemies are in view and close together.
Trigger Combat Focus and take them down one by one, starting with the nearest.
Keep firing through the slow time — don't let the focus end with targets left.
Down five in the single use and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Packed story shootouts are ideal — retry from a checkpoint if the group scatters before you finish.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is the Vice City airport, and an unscheduled departure means taking a plane that isn't on the board — steal one and fly it out. Get onto the tarmac, find a small plane, get in and take off before security stops you. It is a quick, fun trophy once you know the airport layout.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
steps: Drive to VCIA and find a way onto the airfield.
Look for a small plane parked on the tarmac or near a hangar.
Get in the plane and start the engine quickly.
Take off down the runway before security reaches you.
Get airborne and clear of the airport for the trophy to pop.
trophies.tip: Go in with a fast car to cross the tarmac quickly — on foot, security catches you before you reach a plane.

trophies.guide: Rhinos are the game's tanks, and this trophy is about dealing with them — surviving the heat they bring. The exact trigger is a tank encounter, so head for the military areas or the missions where Rhinos appear, and handle the encounter the game sets up. It is a short trophy once you find a Rhino.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
steps: Head for the areas where Rhinos appear, such as the military base.
Approach the tank encounter the game presents.
Use cover and heavy weapons — a tank shrugs off small arms.
Deal with the Rhino threat as the objective directs.
Complete the encounter and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Bring explosives or a heavy rifle: small arms barely scratch a Rhino, and the fight drags on.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: A clean jewelry store robbery means in and out with nobody raising the alarm. Case the store first, go in quiet, take the goods without being spotted by staff or cameras, and leave before anyone notices. If the alarm trips, leave and try again — a detected run doesn't count.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
steps: Find a jewelry store and watch its layout and staff patrols first.
Enter quietly and avoid the staff's line of sight.
Take the goods from the displays without triggering an alarm.
Leave the store the way you came, still undetected.
Get clear of the area and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Go at a quiet hour and move slowly inside — running past staff is what gets you spotted.

trophies.guide: Bank vaults are the big robberies: five of them, each with its own plan, crew and escape. This silver trophy needs all five done and escaped cleanly. Treat each vault like a small heist — prep, entry, grab, getaway — and don't rush the escapes, which is where most runs fail.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
steps: Find the first bank vault target and plan your approach and getaway route.
Enter the bank, reach the vault and grab the take.
Escape the bank and lose the wanted level before it maxes out.
Repeat for the remaining four vaults, one at a time.
Rob and escape all five vaults and the silver trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: The escape matters more than the entry: plan the getaway car and route before you walk in.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks drive set routes around the state. Ram one to a stop or block it, take the crew down, grab the cash, and escape before the cops box you in. It is the classic GTA robbery in miniature and a good warm-up for the bank vaults.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
steps: Find an armored truck on its route around the city.
Ram it or block the road to force it to stop.
Deal with the crew and open the back of the truck.
Grab the cash from inside.
Escape and lose the wanted level for the trophy to pop.
trophies.tip: A heavy car makes the ram easy — use a truck or SUV so the armored truck stops instead of pushing you aside.

trophies.guide: Leonida has 52 named areas, and this trophy needs you to set foot in every one. The map tracks which areas you have visited, so work through it region by region: Vice City, the Keys, the swamps and the countryside. It pairs perfectly with the meditation spots and WAiNK locations, which sit in the same places.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
steps: Open the map and note the 52 named areas across Leonida.
Drive region by region, entering each named area at least once.
Use the map's visited shading to spot the areas you haven't reached.
Cover the Keys and the swamps last — they are the easiest to miss.
Enter all 52 areas and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Combine this with the 18 meditation spots and the WAiNK tour — one route can clear all three trophies.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Nine gangs run illegal operations across Leonida, and this trophy needs one robbery from each gang's operation. Each operation is a defended site, so go in armed, clear it, take the goods and get out. Work through the gangs one at a time and use the tracker to note which ones are done.
trophies.name: Pest Control
steps: Find an illegal operation site and note which gang runs it.
Go in armed and clear the defenders.
Take the operation's goods or cash.
Escape the site and lose any wanted level.
Rob one operation for each of the 9 gangs and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Operations are spread across the map — do them during the exploration sweep so the travel does double duty.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Ocean Beach has a bar with a view, and this trophy is as simple as it sounds: go there, order a cocktail, and enjoy it. It is the most relaxing trophy on the list and a good breather between the harder ones.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
steps: Drive to Ocean Beach on the Vice City waterfront.
Find the beach bar with the ocean view.
Order a cocktail from the bar.
Sit or stand with the drink and the view for a moment.
Finish the drink and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Do this on the way to a WAiNK spot on Ocean Beach — the view is the same and the trip counts twice.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: A vehicle showroom is a glass-fronted shop full of cars, and the classic style is to drive one straight out through the glass. Pick a showroom, get in a car inside, and smash out through the front. It is loud, messy and exactly what the trophy wants.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
steps: Find a vehicle showroom with a glass front.
Get inside and into one of the display cars.
Start the car and aim for the front glass.
Drive straight out through the showroom front.
Escape the scene and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Pick the car nearest the glass so you build speed inside — a slow roll won't break through.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: The Kolt & Associates bowling alley is the game's bowling venue. Go there, play a frame, and follow through on your throw — the trophy pops when you complete the bowling visit. It is one of the easiest trophies and counts toward the activity sampler too.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
steps: Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Walk in and start a game of bowling.
Take your turn and bowl the ball down the lane.
Complete the frame or game the alley offers.
Finish the visit and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Bowling also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None — do it as part of that sampler.

trophies.guide: This trophy is about a partnership moment that lands with the public — a story or side beat where the duo's chemistry wins the crowd. It unlocks through play rather than a grind: follow the story and the partner missions, and the moment comes. If it hasn't popped by the end of the story, check the partner side content you may have skipped.
trophies.name: Personal Best
steps: Play the story and the partner missions as they appear.
Look for the partnership beats the game flags — public moments, not private ones.
Complete the mission or scene that carries the partnership moment.
Let the scene play out to its end.
The trophy unlocks as the moment lands.
trophies.tip: Partner missions are the key: if this hasn't popped, work through any partner side content left in the tracker.

trophies.guide: PlayStation tracks a count for this one, up to 500 — it is about the choices you make across the game, for better or worse. Every meaningful decision, dialogue choice and moral call adds to it, so it fills in naturally over a full playthrough. Don't try to grind it alone; just make choices as you play and check the count in the stats.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
steps: Play the story and make the dialogue and moral choices as they come.
Take the side content too — stranger missions and activities all carry choices.
Check the tracked count in the game's stats to see your progress.
Keep choosing through the late game; the count climbs steadily.
Reach the count the game tracks and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: This one is a marathon, not a sprint — it fills in across the whole game, so don't chase it before the story is done.

trophies.guide: This trophy is about a second attempt succeeding — a retry that lands. It pops when something you failed once works the second time, so it usually unlocks on its own during normal play, especially in the tougher missions or challenges. If it hasn't popped by the late game, retry a challenge you failed once and finish it.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
steps: Play normally — most players earn this the first time a retry lands.
If a mission or challenge fails, retry it straight away.
Finish the retried attempt successfully.
The trophy recognises the second-time success.
It pops as the retry completes.
trophies.tip: Don't force it early: the shooting range and drone races give you plenty of natural second chances.

trophies.guide: This is the game's weird-encounter trophy: something strange happens in Leonida and you witness it. Strange events are scattered around the map — odd scenes, eerie moments, things that don't quite fit — and this trophy pops when you stumble into one. Explore the out-of-the-way places and the odd corners of the state.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
steps: Explore Leonida's odd corners: remote roads, swamps and empty lots.
Watch for strange scenes or events the game doesn't explain.
Approach the event and let it play out.
Stay until the scene finishes.
Witness the strange event and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: The swamps and the Keys hold the strangest sights — tour them at night for the best chance of a weird encounter.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by means striking someone from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon — a bat or similar — and bowling them over. Find a quiet stretch of road, drive slowly past a pedestrian, and swing as you pass. It takes a couple of tries to get the timing, but the trophy pops the moment it connects.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
steps: Get a melee weapon — a bat works best — and a car.
Find a quiet street with pedestrians walking by.
Drive slowly past a pedestrian on the pavement side.
Swing the melee weapon as you draw level with them.
Knock them over with the drive-by and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Slow down to a crawl for the swing — at full speed the timing window is tiny and you'll miss.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are dirty money you pick up from robberies and jobs, and your contacts can launder them clean — for a cut. Keep laundering through the same contacts and the total climbs. Robberies, vaults and armored trucks all feed the marked-bill pile, so this trophy fills in as you do the combat trophies.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
steps: Earn Marked Bills from robberies, vaults and jobs.
Open your contacts and find the laundering option.
Launder the bills through a contact and collect the clean cash.
Repeat after every big robbery so the bills never sit idle.
Launder $250,000 in total and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Launder after every vault and truck robbery — the totals add up fast and you never have to grind it separately.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — weapons, clothes, cars, food, anything the shops sell. It counts cumulatively across the whole game, so normal play covers most of it: ammo, armour, outfits and car upgrades all count. If you're short near the end, buy a big-ticket item like a car.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
steps: Buy ammo, armour and weapons at Ammu-Nation as you play.
Pick up clothes, food and car upgrades from the shops you pass.
Check your spending total in the stats to see how far along you are.
If you're short late in the game, buy a car or a high-end outfit.
Spend $100,000 in total and the trophy pops.
trophies.tip: Car upgrades are the fastest way to close the gap — one good upgrade can cover the last $20,000.

trophies.guide: There are 8 garage properties for sale across Leonida, and this trophy needs all of them bought. Garages are useful as well as collectible — they store your cars — so buy them as you can afford them through the story, and finish the last ones with robbery money in the endgame.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
steps: Check the property listings for the garage properties on sale.
Buy the cheapest garages first, as your story income allows.
Store a car in each garage you buy so it earns its keep.
Use robbery and laundering money for the expensive garages.
Buy all 8 garage properties and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Garages also make the vehicle trophies easier — park your discoveries there instead of losing them.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Scooter Bros is the delivery app, and it lets you register vehicles to it. Find ten different vehicles, open the app, and register each one. Any vehicle you drive can be registered, so this is a quick trophy that pairs with the 100-vehicle discovery hunt.
trophies.name: On the Spot
steps: Drive a vehicle you haven't registered yet.
Open the Scooter Bros app on your phone.
Choose the register option and add the vehicle.
Repeat with nine more different vehicles.
Register 10 vehicles and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: Register every new discovery as you find it for Whip It Good — the two trophies share the same driving.
